title: Taken in Place of the Firstborn

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "They are the Israelites who are to be given wholly to me. I have taken them as my own in place of the firstborn, the first male offspring from every Israelite woman. Every firstborn male in Israel, whether human or animal, is mine. When I struck down all the firstborn in Egypt, I set them apart for myself. And I have taken the Levites in place of all the firstborn sons in Israel." - Num 8:16-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God explains again why the Levites belong to Him: they were taken in place of the firstborn of Israel. On the night of the Passover, when judgment fell on Egypt, God spared Israel's firstborn. From then on, the firstborn belonged to Him. Now the Levites stand in their place, given wholly to God.

At the heart of this is the theme of substitution — one taken in place of another. The whole tribe of Levi was substituted for the firstborn sons of the nation. It is a pattern that runs all through the Bible, and it always points us toward the gospel.

For on the night of Passover, it was the blood of the lamb on the doorframes that caused death to "pass over" Israel's homes. The firstborn were spared because a lamb died in their place. And that lamb pointed forward to Jesus, "the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world" (John 1:29).

Just as the Levites were taken in place of the firstborn, and the lamb died in place of the household, so Christ was taken in our place. He is our substitute, bearing our judgment so that we might be spared and belong to God. "Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed" (1 Cor 5:7).

Rest today in the wonder of substitution. Someone stood in your place. Because of Christ, you have been spared and claimed as God's own.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What does it mean to you that Christ was "taken in your place"?
- How does the Passover picture point you to Jesus?
- How does belonging to God through substitution change how you live?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, my Passover Lamb, thank You for being taken in my place, bearing my judgment so that I could be spared and belong to God. Amen.
